apps.name: Daraja Compass
apps.next: Nothing waiting on you. Ran Jerry's two-clean-runs ask on 15 Nov: drove the app end to end at phone width through all 20 steps of testers/scripts/compass.json, twice in a row, in a test copy (?dj_sandbox=1). BOTH RUNS CLEAN — every step matched what the script says you should see, and zero JavaScript errors in either run. Nothing was broken, so nothing was changed, so the version stamp stays v1.7 · 2026-10-11 and no video needed re-recording. WHAT WAS COVERED: skip the tour, start fresh, Kenya, all 15 questions by typing and by tapping the suggested answers, skipping a question and going back, the five-year picture, walking backward, writing the This month step, saving, ticking it off (GOALS MET went 0/18 to 1/18 with the star), the print view, reloading to check it persists, and working with the network off. node shop/checkvideos.js compass passes 3 of 3, and the shop card still matches the app — name, one-line description, Free, and the same v1.7 · 2026-10-11 stamp as the footer. NO TEST-LIST ITEMS: nothing turned up that needs a human tester beyond what the script already covers, so the tester pack chat was deliberately not sent anything. The script itself is accurate against v1.7 and needs no edits. ONE THING THAT COSTS TIME IF YOU DO NOT KNOW IT, for whoever drives this app next: the tour and first-run cards are attached to <html>, not <body>, on purpose — a comment at index.html line 2003 explains it, the tour sits outside the Aa text-size zoom so its highlight ring is not scaled. The side effect is that document.body.innerText cannot see those cards, so a script that reads body text will think the screen is empty. Read document.documentElement.innerText instead. That is shared house-layer behaviour, in 53 apps, not a Compass fault and not this chat's to change. STILL OPEN, NEITHER URGENT, BOTH THIS CHAT'S WHENEVER THE APP IS NEXT TOUCHED: the store videos pick Kenya for every viewer, which wants revisiting if Compass gets a real US audience; and render() bailing out on needPlace() is a wall for anything driving the app from outside — a tour, a test script, a video — so curing it there rather than line by line would stop that coming back.
